question: At what rate of simple interest will a sum of ₹4,500 amount to ₹5,310 after 4 years?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Simple Interest for 4 years = ₹5,310 − ₹4,500 = ₹810

Simple Interest for 1 year = 810 ÷ 4 = ₹202.5

Rate % = (1-year Interest ÷ Principal) × 100

Rate % = (202.5 ÷ 4500) × 100 = 4.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 4.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹4,500

Amount (A) = ₹5,310

Time (T) = 4 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Amount (A) = P + SI

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3be056a4c94901609997a3b6a443ea095526f3af04a0530e97522e0040e0f9f0.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI = A − P

⇒ SI = 5310 − 4500 = ₹810

⇒ 810 = (4500 × R × 4) ÷ 100

⇒ 810 = 45 × R × 4

⇒ 810 = 180 × R

⇒ R = 810 ÷ 180

⇒ R = 4.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 4.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest

When interest is compounded annually, Amount A = P × (1 + R÷100)T.

SI vs CI Difference

For 2 years, the difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest on the same principal is P × (R÷100)².

Rule of 72

A simple rule to estimate the number of years required to double the invested money at a given annual interest rate (Time ≈ 72 ÷ R).
